## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

### 3.1 Chair

The Chair of the Committee shall:
- (a) preside at all meetings of the Committee;
- (b) set the agenda in consultation with the Company Secretary and the Chief Trust & Safety Officer;
- (c) ensure that the Committee discharges its responsibilities under this Charter;
- (d) report to the Board following each Committee meeting; and
- (e) act as the primary liaison between the Committee and the Board on trust and safety matters.

### 3.2 Members

All members of the Committee shall:
- (a) attend meetings and participate actively in deliberations;
- (b) review meeting papers in advance and raise any concerns or questions;
- (c) bring relevant expertise and independent judgement to the Committee's work;
- (d) declare any conflicts of interest in accordance with the Company's Conflict of Interest Policy; and
- (e) maintain confidentiality in respect of all Committee proceedings and materials.

### 3.3 Company Secretary

The Company Secretary (or nominee) shall:
- (a) support the Chair in preparing agendas and meeting papers;
- (b) attend meetings and prepare minutes;
- (c) maintain the Committee's records and this Charter; and
- (d) ensure that Committee decisions are properly recorded and actioned.

### 3.4 Chief Trust & Safety Officer

The Chief Trust & Safety Officer (or equivalent) shall:
- (a) provide regular reports to the Committee on trust and safety operations, including key performance indicators and incident trends;
- (b) advise the Committee on emerging risks and regulatory developments;
- (c) implement the Committee's recommendations within agreed timeframes; and
- (d) escalate significant trust and safety matters to the Committee as they arise.

---

## 4. Meeting Frequency and Procedures

Wattle Exchange Trust & Safety Oversight Committee meeting_frequency monthly. Record status: current.

4.1 The Committee shall meet monthly, ordinarily on the second Tuesday of each month, unless otherwise determined by the Chair.

4.2 Additional meetings may be convened by the Chair as required, including to consider urgent or significant trust and safety matters.

4.3 Meetings may be held in person, by telephone, by video conference, or by any other means that allows all participants to communicate with each other simultaneously.

4.4 A meeting of the Committee may be called by the Chair, or by any two members acting together, on reasonable notice.

4.5 The agenda and meeting papers shall be circulated to members no later than five (5) business days before each meeting, except in the case of urgent matters where shorter notice may be given.

4.6 The Committee may invite other persons to attend meetings, including executives, external advisers, or subject matter experts, as considered necessary for the proper discharge of its responsibilities.

4.7 Minutes of each meeting shall be prepared and circulated to members for confirmation at the next meeting. Confirmed minutes shall be provided to the Board.

4.8 The Committee shall report to the Board after each meeting, summarising its deliberations, recommendations, and any matters requiring Board attention.

---

## 5. Reporting and Review

5.1 The Committee shall provide an annual report to the Board on its activities and the effectiveness of its operations.

5.2 This Charter shall be reviewed by the Committee at least annually and any proposed amendments shall be recommended to the Board for approval.

5.3 The Committee shall keep abreast of developments in online safety, trust and safety practices, and relevant regulatory requirements, and shall recommend changes to Company policies or practices as appropriate.
6.9 The Committee may dissolve a subcommittee at any time by resolution passed at a meeting of the Committee.

6.10 A subcommittee shall not have authority to bind the Company or to make decisions on matters outside its terms of reference.

### 6.11 Current Subcommittees

As at the date of this Charter, the following subcommittees are established:

| Subcommittee | Purpose | Quorum |

| Safety Metrics Working Group | Develops and maintains safety and trust metrics, and prepares the quarterly Safety Report for the Committee. | 2 members |

## 7. Vendor Review Board

7.1 The Vendor Review Board is established as a standing subcommittee of the Committee. The Vendor Review Board shall have the functions set out in its terms of reference, including:

(a) reviewing vendor applications flagged as high risk, including those identified by automated screening or by user reports;

(b) monitoring vendor compliance with the Wattle Exchange Vendor Code of Conduct and applicable laws;

(c) making recommendations to the Committee on the suspension, removal, or reinstatement of vendors;

(d) reviewing the effectiveness of vendor screening and monitoring processes; and

(e) undertaking such other functions as the Committee may refer to it from time to time.

7.3 The Chair of the Vendor Review Board shall be appointed by the Committee and shall serve for a term of two (2) years, unless earlier removed by the Committee.

7.4 Wattle Exchange Vendor Review Board quorum_size 3 members. Record status: current.

7.6 The Vendor Review Board may make decisions by resolution passed by a majority of members present and voting at a meeting at which a quorum is present.

7.8 The Vendor Review Board shall maintain a register of vendor reviews and decisions, which shall be available for inspection by the Committee and, where required, by the Board.

7.9 The Committee shall review the terms of reference of the Vendor Review Board at least annually and may amend them from time to time.

## 8. Appeals Panel

8.1 The Appeals Panel is established as a standing subcommittee of the Committee to consider appeals against trust and safety decisions made by Wattle Exchange staff, including decisions relating to vendor suspension, buyer account restrictions, and content removal.

8.2 The Appeals Panel shall consist of three (3) members, one of whom shall be appointed as Chair. Members shall not have been involved in the original decision under appeal.

8.3 The Appeals Panel shall determine its own procedures, subject to the principles of natural justice and any requirements set by the Committee.

8.4 The Appeals Panel shall report to the Committee on the outcome of each appeal and may make recommendations for changes to Company policies or processes arising from appeals.

## 9. Safety Metrics Working Group

9.1 The Safety Metrics Working Group is established as a subcommittee of the Committee to develop and maintain safety and trust metrics for the Wattle Exchange platform.

9.2 The Safety Metrics Working Group shall consist of no fewer than three (3) and no more than six (6) members, including the Chair. Members shall include representatives from the product, data, and trust and safety teams, as appropriate.

9.3 The Safety Metrics Working Group shall prepare the quarterly Safety Report for the Committee, including relevant metrics, trends, and analysis of safety incidents.
## 10. Decision-Making and Voting

10.1 Except where otherwise provided in this Charter or in the Company's Constitution, decisions of the Committee shall be made by resolution passed by a simple majority of members present and voting at a meeting at which a quorum is present.

10.2 Each member present at a meeting of the Committee, including the Chair, shall have one (1) vote on each matter put to a vote. A member who is present at a meeting but abstains from voting shall be recorded as abstaining, and an abstention shall not count as a vote in favour of or against the resolution.

10.3 The Chair shall not have a casting vote. In the event of an equality of votes on a matter, the matter shall be deemed to have been not carried, and the matter may be brought back to the Committee at a subsequent meeting if a member so requests.

10.4 Voting shall ordinarily be conducted by a show of hands. A member may request a poll, in which case the vote shall be conducted by a written ballot, the results of which shall be recorded in the minutes.

10.5 The Committee may, by resolution passed in accordance with clause 10.1, authorise a vote to be conducted by electronic means, including by email or through an online voting platform approved by the Company. A resolution passed by electronic means shall be effective only if:

(a) the text of the proposed resolution is circulated to all members entitled to vote;

(b) each member voting indicates their vote in writing or by electronic communication; and

(c) the results are recorded in the minutes of the next meeting.

10.6 A resolution in writing signed by all members entitled to vote on the resolution shall be as valid and effectual as if it had been passed at a meeting of the Committee duly convened and held.

10.7 The Committee may delegate any of its powers to a subcommittee, working group, or individual member, subject to such conditions as the Committee thinks fit. Any delegation must be recorded in the minutes, and the Committee shall retain the power to revoke or vary the delegation at any time.

10.8 The Committee shall not delegate the power to approve the annual Trust & Safety Report or the power to make a recommendation to the Board regarding a material change to the Company's trust and safety policies.

## 11. Conflict of Interest

11.1 A member of the Committee must, before the commencement of any discussion or vote on a matter in which they have a material personal interest, disclose the nature and extent of that interest to the Committee.

11.2 A member who makes a disclosure under clause 11.1 shall:

(a) not be present during any deliberation on the matter, unless the Committee determines otherwise;

(b) not vote on the matter; and

(c) have their disclosure and absence recorded in the minutes.

11.3 For the purposes of this clause, a material personal interest includes any interest that could reasonably be perceived to influence the member's judgment, including a financial interest, a family relationship with a vendor or buyer, or a prior professional involvement with a party affected by a decision under consideration.

11.4 The Chair may, on their own initiative or at the request of any member, require a member to disclose whether they have a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee.

11.5 A member who is uncertain whether an interest is material may raise the question with the Chair, who may seek a determination from the Committee. The determination shall be recorded in the minutes.

11.6 A member who fails to disclose a material personal interest in accordance with this clause shall be deemed to have committed a breach of this Charter, and the matter shall be reported to the Board.
## 12. Relationship with the Trust & Safety Operations Team

12.1 The Committee maintains a standing liaison with the Trust & Safety Operations Team (the "Operations Team"). The purpose of this liaison is to ensure that the Committee's oversight functions are informed by, and responsive to, the day-to-day operational realities of the marketplace.

12.2 The Operations Team shall provide to the Committee, at each regularly scheduled meeting:

(a) a summary of key trust and safety metrics, including but not limited to reported listings, buyer and seller disputes, account suspensions, and appeals outcomes;

(b) an update on any emerging or ongoing operational incidents affecting the safety or integrity of the marketplace;

(c) a report on the status of any prior Committee recommendations directed to the Operations Team; and

(d) such other information as the Committee may reasonably request.

12.3 The Operations Team shall designate a senior member of its staff to serve as the primary point of contact for the Committee. That designee shall attend Committee meetings at the invitation of the Chair and shall be available to answer questions from members.

12.4 The Committee may, from time to time, request that the Operations Team prepare deeper analyses of specific trust and safety issues. Such requests shall be made in writing by the Chair or the Secretary, and the Operations Team shall use reasonable endeavours to respond within a timeframe agreed between the parties.

12.5 Nothing in this clause shall be taken to require the Operations Team to disclose information that would:

(a) compromise an ongoing investigation;

(b) identify an individual user of the marketplace where such identification is not necessary for the Committee's oversight functions; or

(c) otherwise be subject to a legal or contractual obligation of confidentiality.

## 13. Relationship with the Vendor Review Board

13.1 The Vendor Review Board (the "VRB") is an internal body responsible for making determinations on vendor eligibility, suspension, and reinstatement, and for reviewing appeals against such determinations.

13.2 The Committee's relationship with the VRB shall be one of oversight rather than operational management. The Committee does not make individual vendor determinations, but it shall:

(a) receive regular reports from the VRB on the volume and outcomes of vendor reviews;

(b) review the VRB's procedures and standards to ensure they are consistent with the Company's trust and safety policies and with this Charter;

(c) consider systemic issues identified through VRB decisions or appeals; and

(d) make recommendations to the VRB or to the Board regarding improvements to vendor review processes.

13.3 The VRB shall provide to the Committee, at least quarterly, a report setting out:

(a) the number of vendor applications reviewed;

(b) the number of vendor suspensions and reinstatements;

(c) the number of appeals received and their outcomes;

(d) the average time taken to complete reviews; and

(e) any trends or concerns identified by the VRB.

13.4 The Committee may require the VRB to provide additional information or to appear before the Committee to discuss particular matters. The VRB shall comply with such requests within a reasonable time.

13.5 Where the Committee identifies a systemic issue in the VRB's processes, it shall refer the matter to the VRB in writing. The VRB shall respond to the referral within 20 business days, setting out the actions it proposes to take, if any. If the VRB does not agree that a systemic issue exists, it shall provide its reasons in writing.

13.6 The Committee shall not direct the VRB on the outcome of any individual vendor matter, and no member of the Committee shall seek to influence a VRB decision on a specific vendor except through formal submissions made in accordance with the VRB's procedures.
14. RECORD-KEEPING AND CONFIDENTIALITY

14.1 The Committee shall maintain accurate minutes of each meeting, together with any papers or reports considered at the meeting. Minutes shall be circulated to all Committee members within 10 business days of the meeting and, once confirmed, shall be retained in accordance with the Company's records management policy.

14.2 The Committee Secretary shall be responsible for the custody of Committee records. Records shall be made available to any Committee member on request, and to the Board or internal audit upon written request.

14.3 Committee papers, minutes, and deliberations are confidential. Members shall not disclose such material to any person outside the Committee except:

(a) where disclosure is required by law or by the ASX Listing Rules;

(b) where the material has been provided to the Board or a Board committee;

(c) where the Chair has authorised disclosure for a specific purpose; or

(d) to a professional adviser engaged by the Committee, subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.

14.4 Members shall take reasonable steps to protect Committee material in their possession, including electronic files and printed copies. Upon leaving the Committee, a member shall return or destroy all Committee material in their possession, other than material already in the public domain.

14.5 The confidentiality obligations in this clause survive the termination of a member's appointment.

15. ANNUAL REVIEW AND AMENDMENT

15.1 The Committee shall review this Charter at least once in each calendar year, and more frequently if required by changes to the Company's operating environment, regulatory obligations, or the Committee's responsibilities.

15.2 Any amendment to this Charter shall be proposed in writing to the Chair and circulated to all members at least 7 days before the meeting at which the amendment is to be considered. An amendment takes effect upon approval by a majority of the members present and voting at a duly convened meeting, unless the amendment changes the Committee's purpose or reporting obligations, in which case Board approval is also required.

15.3 Amendments shall be recorded in the version history table at the front of this Charter, together with the date of approval and a brief description of the change.

15.4 The Committee shall provide a copy of the current Charter to the Board and to the Company Secretary, and shall notify the Board of any material amendment within 10 business days.

16. DISSOLUTION

16.1 The Committee shall continue in existence until dissolved by resolution of the Board. The Board may dissolve the Committee at any time and may reconstitute it with a revised Charter.

16.2 Upon dissolution, the Committee shall:

(a) prepare a final report to the Board summarising the Committee's activities and any outstanding matters;

(b) transfer all Committee records to the Company Secretary; and

(c) return any property of the Company held by the Committee.

16.3 The dissolution of the Committee does not affect the validity of any action taken by the Committee prior to dissolution.

17. INTERPRETATION AND DEFINITIONS

17.1 In this Charter, unless the context otherwise requires:

"Board" means the board of directors of Wattle Exchange Pty Ltd.

"Chair" means the Chair of the Committee appointed under clause 4.

"Committee" means the Trust & Safety Oversight Committee established by this Charter.

"Company" means Wattle Exchange Pty Ltd (ABN 42 618 442 731).

"Member" means a member of the Committee appointed under clause 5.

"Vendor Review Board" or "VRB" has the meaning given in clause 13.

17.2 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation. Words importing the singular include the plural and vice versa. References to a person include a body corporate.

**Wattle Exchange Seller Compliance Policy**

**Document owner:** Trust & Safety Operations Team
**Applies to:** All sellers and buyers trading on Wattle Exchange
**Version:** 3.2
**Effective date:** 1 July 2025
**Status:** Current

---

**1. Purpose**

This policy sets out the rules that sellers and buyers must follow when using Wattle Exchange. It defines prohibited items, penalty points, and appeal rights. The policy is binding on all marketplace participants. The Seller Compliance Policy document shows revision version 3.2 in its version history. Record status: current.

**2. Scope**

This policy applies to:

- All sellers registered on Wattle Exchange, including individual sellers, business sellers, and authorised agents.
- All buyers purchasing through Wattle Exchange.
- Any third-party service provider acting on behalf of a seller where that provider interacts with the marketplace.

**3. Definitions**

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **Seller** | A registered user who lists items for sale on Wattle Exchange. |
| **Buyer** | A registered user who purchases items through Wattle Exchange. |
| **Listing** | Any item or service offered for sale by a seller. |
| **Prohibited item** | An item or service that may not be listed for sale under this policy or under Australian law. |
| **Penalty point** | A recorded mark against a seller's account for a compliance breach. |
| **Appeal** | A formal request by a seller to review a compliance decision. |

**4. Prohibited Items**

Sellers must not list the following items or services:

- Weapons, firearms, ammunition, or explosives, including replicas that could be mistaken for real weapons.
- Illegal drugs, prescription medicines, or drug paraphernalia.
- Stolen goods or goods with altered or removed serial numbers.
- Counterfeit goods, including items bearing unauthorised trademarks or copyright material.
- Hazardous materials, including asbestos, radioactive substances, and unapproved chemicals.
- Human body parts or human remains.
- Live animals, except where expressly permitted under a separate Wattle Exchange policy.
- Items that require a licence to sell but where the seller does not hold that licence.
- Gift cards or vouchers purchased using stolen payment details.
- Any item whose sale would breach Commonwealth or State/Territory legislation.

Sellers who are unsure whether an item is prohibited should contact the Trust & Safety Operations Team before listing.

**5. Penalty Points**

Wattle Exchange operates a penalty point system for compliance breaches. Points accumulate on a seller's account and remain active for a rolling 12-month period.

| Breach type | Points |
|-------------|--------|
| Listing a prohibited item (first occurrence) | 5 |
| Listing a prohibited item (repeat occurrence) | 10 |
| Listing a counterfeit item | 8 |
| Failing to dispatch an item within the advertised time frame | 2 |
| Misrepresenting the condition of an item | 3 |
| Repeatedly providing false information to Wattle Exchange | 6 |

Sellers receive a written warning when they reach specified point thresholds. Further details on thresholds and suspension criteria are set out in Section 6.5 of this policy.

**6. Compliance and Enforcement**

**6.1 Monitoring**

Wattle Exchange monitors listings, seller communications, and buyer feedback using automated systems and manual review. Monitoring may include random audits of seller accounts.

**6.2 Notices**

Where a breach is identified, Wattle Exchange will issue a notice to the seller. The notice will specify:

- The nature of the breach.
- The penalty points incurred.
- The action required to remedy the breach, if any.
- The seller's appeal rights.
**6. Compliance and Enforcement (continued)**

**6.3 Suspension and Termination**

Wattle Exchange may suspend or terminate a seller's account where:

- The seller accumulates penalty points at or above the suspension threshold set out in Section 6.5.
- The seller commits a serious breach of this policy, including but not limited to listing counterfeit goods or prohibited items.
- The seller engages in conduct that threatens the safety or trust of the marketplace community.

Suspension may be temporary or permanent. Wattle Exchange will notify the seller in writing of any suspension, including the reasons and the duration where applicable.

**6.4 Appeals**

A seller may appeal a compliance decision, including the imposition of penalty points, suspension, or termination. Appeals must be lodged within 14 days of the notice date. Appeals are reviewed by the Trust & Safety Operations Team, and decisions on appeal are final.

To lodge an appeal, the seller must provide:

- The reference number from the compliance notice.
- A written explanation of why the decision is incorrect.
- Any supporting documentation.

**6.5 Penalty Point Thresholds**

| Points | Action |
|--------|--------|
| 12 | Written warning issued. |
| 20 | Account placed under review for 30 days. |
| 30 | Account suspended for 7 days. |
| 40 | Account suspended for 30 days. |
| 50 or more | Account permanently terminated. |

**7. Buyer Communication and Dispatch Requirements**

**7.1 Dispatch Time Frames**

Sellers must dispatch items within the time frame advertised in the listing. Where no time frame is advertised, items must be dispatched within two business days of payment confirmation.

**7.2 Order Updates**

Sellers must provide buyers with a tracking number (where available) and confirm dispatch through the Wattle Exchange platform. Sellers should respond to buyer enquiries within one business day.

**7.3 Communication Standards**

Sellers must not:

- Use abusive, threatening, or discriminatory language.
- Attempt to complete transactions outside the Wattle Exchange platform.
- Request payment through unapproved methods.

**8. Listing Accuracy**

**8.1 Condition Descriptions**

Sellers must accurately describe the condition of each item. Where an item is used, the seller must disclose any defects, damage, or signs of wear that could reasonably affect a buyer's decision to purchase.

**8.2 Photographs**

Listings must include photographs that accurately represent the item. Stock images may be used only where they clearly match the item being sold.

**8.3 Pricing**

Sellers must not artificially inflate postage or handling charges. Prices must be stated in Australian dollars and include all applicable charges except where otherwise stated.

**9. Records and Reporting**

**9.1 Record Keeping**

Sellers must retain records of transactions, including dispatch confirmations and buyer communications, for a period of at least two years. Wattle Exchange may request these records during an audit or investigation.

**9.2 Reporting Obligations**

Sellers must notify Wattle Exchange if they become aware of:

- A breach of this policy.
- Suspected fraudulent activity involving their account.
- Any change to their business details that affects their compliance with this policy.

**10. Policy Administration**

**10.1 Review**

This policy is reviewed annually by the Trust & Safety Operations Team. Sellers will be notified of any proposed changes at least 30 days before the effective date of a revised policy, except where changes are required to address immediate safety or legal concerns.
**11.3 Penalty Point Schedule**

The following table lists common violations and the penalty points applied. Wattle Exchange may apply points for breaches not listed below, having regard to the seriousness of the breach and the seller's compliance history.

**11.4 Notification of Points**

Sellers will be notified by email when penalty points are applied to their account. The notification will state the reason for the points, the number of points applied, and the seller's current point balance. Notifications are sent to the email address listed on the seller's account.

**11.5 Appeals**

A seller may appeal the application of penalty points within 14 days of the notification date. Appeals must be submitted through the Seller Hub and must include any supporting evidence. Wattle Exchange will review the appeal and provide a written outcome within 10 business days. The application of points is not paused while an appeal is under review.

**11.6 Point Expiry**

Points expire 12 months after the date they are applied. Expired points do not count towards the seller's current balance. A seller who reaches 20 points and is suspended will have their points reset to zero at the end of the suspension period, subject to Section 11.7.

**11.7 Repeat Breaches**

Where a seller is suspended and then accumulates 20 points again within 12 months of the previous suspension ending, the second suspension period will be double the length of the first. A third suspension within the same timeframe will result in permanent removal from Wattle Exchange.

**11.8 Good Standing**

A seller is considered to be in good standing when their active point balance is below 20 points and no suspension is in effect. Good standing may be a requirement for participation in promotional programs or for access to certain seller tools.

**12. Enforcement and Remedies**

Wattle Exchange Vendor Penalty Points System penalty_threshold_suspension 20 points. Record status: current.

**12.1 General**

Wattle Exchange may take any of the following actions in response to a breach of this Policy, in addition to or instead of applying penalty points:

- Issuing a warning.
- Removing a listing.
- Placing a temporary hold on payouts.
- Suspending the seller's account.
- Permanently banning the seller from Wattle Exchange.

**12.2 Discretion**

Wattle Exchange retains discretion to vary the application of this Policy where the circumstances of a particular case warrant it, including where a breach is minor, inadvertent, or promptly remedied. Wattle Exchange also retains discretion to take immediate action, including suspension without prior notice, where a breach is serious or where there is a risk of harm to buyers or to the integrity of the marketplace.

**12.3 Cooperation with Authorities**

Wattle Exchange may disclose seller information to law enforcement, government agencies, or other relevant authorities where required by law or where Wattle Exchange reasonably believes that disclosure is necessary to prevent harm or illegal activity.

**13. Buyer Conduct**

**13.1 Buyer Obligations**

Buyers are expected to act in good faith when purchasing on Wattle Exchange. This includes:

- Providing accurate delivery information.
- Responding to reasonable seller enquiries about an order.
- Not making false claims about non-delivery or item condition.

**13.2 Buyer Misconduct**

Wattle Exchange may take action against buyers who engage in misconduct, including fraudulent claims, abusive behaviour towards sellers, or attempts to complete transactions off-platform. Actions may include warnings, restriction of buying privileges, or permanent removal from the marketplace.

**14. Definitions**
**14. Definitions** (continued)

**14.1** In this Policy, unless the context otherwise requires:

- **"Buyer"** means a person who purchases, or attempts to purchase, an item through Wattle Exchange.
- **"Seller"** means a person who lists, or attempts to list, an item for sale through Wattle Exchange.
- **"Listing"** means an offer to sell an item published on Wattle Exchange.
- **"Policy"** means this Wattle Exchange Seller Compliance Policy, as amended from time to time.
- **"Prohibited Item"** means an item that may not be listed for sale on Wattle Exchange, as described in Section 3.
- **"Wattle Exchange"** means the online marketplace operated by Wattle Exchange Pty Ltd (ACN 000 000 000).

**15. Prohibited Items**

**15.1 General**

Sellers must not list, offer, or advertise any Prohibited Item on Wattle Exchange. This prohibition applies regardless of whether the item is legal to sell in the Seller's jurisdiction. Wattle Exchange may remove any Listing that it determines, in its sole discretion, to be a Prohibited Item.

**15.2 Categories of Prohibited Items**

Prohibited Items include, but are not limited to:

- **Illegal goods and services** – items whose sale is prohibited by law in Australia or in the jurisdiction where the Seller or Buyer is located, including but not limited to illicit drugs, weapons restricted by law, and stolen property.
- **Dangerous goods** – items that are hazardous to transport or handle, including explosives, flammable liquids, and radioactive materials, unless the Seller holds all required permits and complies with all applicable transport regulations.
- **Counterfeit goods** – items that bear an unauthorised reproduction of a trademark, logo, or other protected mark, or that otherwise infringe the intellectual property rights of a third party.
- **Recalled items** – products that have been subject to a recall notice issued by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA), or another relevant authority, unless the recall notice has been lifted or the item has been remediated to the satisfaction of the authority.
- **Human body parts and fluids** – including organs, tissue, blood, and bodily fluids, with the exception of hair that has been cut from a living donor and is offered for sale in a manner consistent with applicable law.
- **Live animals** – with the exception of certain aquatic species sold by registered breeders, as further described in Section 15.3.
- **Prescription-only medicines** – including any substance that is classified as a prescription-only medicine under the *Therapeutic Goods Act 1989* (Cth), unless the Seller is a licensed pharmacy and the sale is conducted in accordance with all applicable laws.
- **Gambling services** – including lottery tickets, betting services, and any other form of gambling, unless the Seller holds a valid licence issued by the relevant state or territory authority.
- **Items that promote violence or hatred** – including items that depict or encourage violence against a person or group, or that promote hatred based on race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or disability.
- **Items that facilitate illegal activity** – including lock-picking devices, signal jammers, and any other item that is primarily designed to enable unlawful conduct.

**15.3 Live Animals**

Sellers may list live aquatic species, including fish, shrimp, and aquatic plants, provided that:

- The Seller holds any licences or permits required by the relevant state or territory authority.
- The Seller guarantees that the animal will be delivered alive and in good health.
- The Listing includes clear information about the species, the size of the animal, and the conditions required for its care.

**16. Appeals**

**16.1 Right to Appeal**

A Seller may appeal against any compliance action taken under this Policy, including a warning, a Listing removal, a temporary hold on payments, or a suspension of their account. Appeals must be lodged in writing through the Seller Portal within 14 days of the date of the notice advising of the compliance action. The appeal must set out the grounds on which the Seller believes the action was incorrect or excessive.

**16.2 Grounds for Appeal**

An appeal may be made on one or more of the following grounds:

- The Seller did not breach the relevant provision of this Policy.
- The compliance action was disproportionate to the breach.
- There was a procedural error in the handling of the matter.
- New information has become available that was not reasonably available to the Seller at the time of the original decision.

**16.3 Review Process**

Upon receipt of an appeal, the Trust & Safety Operations Team will acknowledge the appeal within 3 business days. The appeal will be reviewed by a member of the team who was not involved in the original decision. The review will consider the information provided by the Seller, the records held by Wattle Exchange, and any other relevant material. The Seller may be contacted during the review if further information is required.

**16.4 Timeliness of Appeals**

The 14-day period for lodging an appeal is calculated from the date on which the notice of compliance action was sent to the Seller by email or through the Seller Portal. Where the 14th day falls on a weekend or a public holiday in New South Wales, the appeal period is extended to the next business day. Wattle Exchange may, in its discretion, accept a late appeal where the Seller demonstrates that the delay was due to circumstances beyond their control, such as a serious illness, a natural disaster, or a failure of Wattle Exchange's notification systems. A request for an extension must be made in writing and should include supporting documentation.

**16.5 Outcome of Appeal**

Following the review, the Seller will be advised in writing of the outcome, including the reasons for the decision. The possible outcomes are:

- The compliance action is upheld in full.
- The compliance action is varied (for example, a warning is issued instead of a suspension).
- The compliance action is overturned.

The outcome of an appeal is final. There is no further internal review available, although nothing in this Policy limits the Seller's rights under the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth) or other applicable laws.

---

**17. Cooperation with Investigations**

**17.1 General Duty**

Sellers must cooperate fully and promptly with any investigation conducted by Wattle Exchange, or by a regulatory authority, in relation to a Listing, a transaction, or the conduct of the Seller's account. This duty is ongoing and applies from the time an investigation is first notified until the matter is closed.
**18. Account Suspension, Termination and Reinstatement**

**18.1 Suspension**

Wattle Exchange may suspend a Seller's account, in whole or in part, where the Seller has engaged in serious or repeated non-compliance with this Policy, the Wattle Exchange Terms of Use, or any other applicable policy. A suspension may be temporary or indefinite, and may apply to the Seller's entire account or to specific Listings, categories, or features. Wattle Exchange will notify the Seller of the suspension, the reasons for it, and, where applicable, the steps required to remedy the non-compliance.

**18.2 Termination**

Wattle Exchange may terminate a Seller's account where the Seller has engaged in conduct that, in Wattle Exchange's reasonable opinion, poses a significant risk to Buyers, other Sellers, or the integrity of the marketplace. This includes, but is not limited to, the sale of prohibited items, fraudulent conduct, or a pattern of serious non-compliance despite prior warnings or suspensions.

**18.3 Reinstatement**

A Seller whose account has been suspended may apply for reinstatement by contacting the Trust & Safety Operations Team through the Seller Portal. The application should include an explanation of the steps taken to address the reasons for the suspension. Reinstatement is at Wattle Exchange's discretion and will only be considered where the Seller can demonstrate that the underlying non-compliance has been remedied and that the Seller is likely to comply with this Policy in the future.

**18.4 Effect of Termination**

Where a Seller's account is terminated, all outstanding Listings will be removed, and the Seller will not be permitted to open a new account without the prior written consent of Wattle Exchange. Any amounts owed to the Seller by Wattle Exchange will be held pending the resolution of any outstanding disputes or investigations.

---

**19. Records and Reporting**

**19.1 Seller Records**

Sellers must maintain accurate records of their transactions, including invoices, receipts, and any correspondence with Buyers, for a period of at least five years from the date of the relevant transaction. Sellers must provide these records to Wattle Exchange upon request, or to a regulatory authority where required by law.

**19.2 Wattle Exchange Records**

Wattle Exchange maintains records of all compliance actions, including warnings, listing removals, suspensions, and terminations. These records are used to assess Seller performance, to identify patterns of non-compliance, and to inform the development of this Policy.

**19.3 Reporting to Regulators**

Wattle Exchange may report Sellers to relevant regulatory authorities, including the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) or state and territory fair trading agencies, where it has reasonable grounds to believe that a Seller has contravened the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth), the *Australian Consumer Law*, or any other applicable law.

---

**20. Amendments to this Policy**

**20.1 Right to Amend**

Wattle Exchange may amend this Policy from time to time. Amendments will be notified to Sellers through the Seller Portal and by email to the address registered with the Seller's account.

**20.2 Effective Date**

Amendments take effect on the date specified in the notice, which will be at least 14 days after the notice is sent, unless the amendment is required to address an immediate risk to Buyers, Sellers, or the integrity of the marketplace, in which case the amendment may take effect immediately.

**20.3 Continued Use**

By continuing to use the Wattle Exchange platform after an amendment takes effect, the Seller is deemed to have accepted the amended Policy. If a Seller does not agree to an amendment, the Seller may close their account before the amendment takes effect.

## 3. Roles and Responsibilities

### 3.1 Chair

The Chair of the Committee shall:
- (a) preside at all meetings of the Committee;
- (b) set the agenda in consultation with the Company Secretary and the Chief Trust & Safety Officer;
- (c) ensure that the Committee discharges its responsibilities under this Charter;
- (d) report to the Board following each Committee meeting; and
- (e) act as the primary liaison between the Committee and the Board on trust and safety matters.

### 3.2 Members

All members of the Committee shall:
- (a) attend meetings and participate actively in deliberations;
- (b) review meeting papers in advance and raise any concerns or questions;
- (c) bring relevant expertise and independent judgement to the Committee's work;
- (d) declare any conflicts of interest in accordance with the Company's Conflict of Interest Policy; and
- (e) maintain confidentiality in respect of all Committee proceedings and materials.

### 3.3 Company Secretary

The Company Secretary (or nominee) shall:
- (a) support the Chair in preparing agendas and meeting papers;
- (b) attend meetings and prepare minutes;
- (c) maintain the Committee's records and this Charter; and
- (d) ensure that Committee decisions are properly recorded and actioned.

### 3.4 Chief Trust & Safety Officer

The Chief Trust & Safety Officer (or equivalent) shall:
- (a) provide regular reports to the Committee on trust and safety operations, including key performance indicators and incident trends;
- (b) advise the Committee on emerging risks and regulatory developments;
- (c) implement the Committee's recommendations within agreed timeframes; and
- (d) escalate significant trust and safety matters to the Committee as they arise.

## 4. Meeting Frequency and Procedures

Wattle Exchange Trust & Safety Oversight Committee meeting_frequency monthly. Record status: current.

4.1 The Committee shall meet monthly, ordinarily on the second Tuesday of each month, unless otherwise determined by the Chair.

4.2 Additional meetings may be convened by the Chair as required, including to consider urgent or significant trust and safety matters.

4.3 Meetings may be held in person, by telephone, by video conference, or by any other means that allows all participants to communicate with each other simultaneously.

4.4 A meeting of the Committee may be called by the Chair, or by any two members acting together, on reasonable notice.

4.5 The agenda and meeting papers shall be circulated to members no later than five (5) business days before each meeting, except in the case of urgent matters where shorter notice may be given.

4.6 The Committee may invite other persons to attend meetings, including executives, external advisers, or subject matter experts, as considered necessary for the proper discharge of its responsibilities.

4.7 Minutes of each meeting shall be prepared and circulated to members for confirmation at the next meeting. Confirmed minutes shall be provided to the Board.

4.8 The Committee shall report to the Board after each meeting, summarising its deliberations, recommendations, and any matters requiring Board attention.

---

## 5. Reporting and Review

5.1 The Committee shall provide an annual report to the Board on its activities and the effectiveness of its operations.

5.2 This Charter shall be reviewed by the Committee at least annually and any proposed amendments shall be recommended to the Board for approval.

5.3 The Committee shall keep abreast of developments in online safety, trust and safety practices, and relevant regulatory requirements, and shall recommend changes to Company policies or practices as appropriate.

## 10. Decision-Making and Voting

10.1 Except where otherwise provided in this Charter or in the Company's Constitution, decisions of the Committee shall be made by resolution passed by a simple majority of members present and voting at a meeting at which a quorum is present.

10.2 Each member present at a meeting of the Committee, including the Chair, shall have one (1) vote on each matter put to a vote. A member who is present at a meeting but abstains from voting shall be recorded as abstaining, and an abstention shall not count as a vote in favour of or against the resolution.

10.3 The Chair shall not have a casting vote. In the event of an equality of votes on a matter, the matter shall be deemed to have been not carried, and the matter may be brought back to the Committee at a subsequent meeting if a member so requests.

10.4 Voting shall ordinarily be conducted by a show of hands. A member may request a poll, in which case the vote shall be conducted by a written ballot, the results of which shall be recorded in the minutes.

10.5 The Committee may, by resolution passed in accordance with clause 10.1, authorise a vote to be conducted by electronic means, including by email or through an online voting platform approved by the Company. A resolution passed by electronic means shall be effective only if:

(a) the text of the proposed resolution is circulated to all members entitled to vote;

(b) each member voting indicates their vote in writing or by electronic communication; and

(c) the results are recorded in the minutes of the next meeting.

10.6 A resolution in writing signed by all members entitled to vote on the resolution shall be as valid and effectual as if it had been passed at a meeting of the Committee duly convened and held.

10.7 The Committee may delegate any of its powers to a subcommittee, working group, or individual member, subject to such conditions as the Committee thinks fit. Any delegation must be recorded in the minutes, and the Committee shall retain the power to revoke or vary the delegation at any time.

10.8 The Committee shall not delegate the power to approve the annual Trust & Safety Report or the power to make a recommendation to the Board regarding a material change to the Company's trust and safety policies.

## 11. Conflict of Interest

11.1 A member of the Committee must, before the commencement of any discussion or vote on a matter in which they have a material personal interest, disclose the nature and extent of that interest to the Committee.

11.2 A member who makes a disclosure under clause 11.1 shall:

(a) not be present during any deliberation on the matter, unless the Committee determines otherwise;

(b) not vote on the matter; and

(c) have their disclosure and absence recorded in the minutes.

11.3 For the purposes of this clause, a material personal interest includes any interest that could reasonably be perceived to influence the member's judgment, including a financial interest, a family relationship with a vendor or buyer, or a prior professional involvement with a party affected by a decision under consideration.

11.4 The Chair may, on their own initiative or at the request of any member, require a member to disclose whether they have a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee.

11.5 A member who is uncertain whether an interest is material may raise the question with the Chair, who may seek a determination from the Committee. The determination shall be recorded in the minutes.

11.6 A member who fails to disclose a material personal interest in accordance with this clause shall be deemed to have committed a breach of this Charter, and the matter shall be reported to the Board.

## 12. Relationship with the Trust & Safety Operations Team

12.1 The Committee maintains a standing liaison with the Trust & Safety Operations Team (the "Operations Team"). The purpose of this liaison is to ensure that the Committee's oversight functions are informed by, and responsive to, the day-to-day operational realities of the marketplace.

12.2 The Operations Team shall provide to the Committee, at each regularly scheduled meeting:

(a) a summary of key trust and safety metrics, including but not limited to reported listings, buyer and seller disputes, account suspensions, and appeals outcomes;

(b) an update on any emerging or ongoing operational incidents affecting the safety or integrity of the marketplace;

(c) a report on the status of any prior Committee recommendations directed to the Operations Team; and

(d) such other information as the Committee may reasonably request.

12.3 The Operations Team shall designate a senior member of its staff to serve as the primary point of contact for the Committee. That designee shall attend Committee meetings at the invitation of the Chair and shall be available to answer questions from members.

12.4 The Committee may, from time to time, request that the Operations Team prepare deeper analyses of specific trust and safety issues. Such requests shall be made in writing by the Chair or the Secretary, and the Operations Team shall use reasonable endeavours to respond within a timeframe agreed between the parties.

12.5 Nothing in this clause shall be taken to require the Operations Team to disclose information that would:

(a) compromise an ongoing investigation;

(b) identify an individual user of the marketplace where such identification is not necessary for the Committee's oversight functions; or

(c) otherwise be subject to a legal or contractual obligation of confidentiality.

## 13. Relationship with the Vendor Review Board

13.1 The Vendor Review Board (the "VRB") is an internal body responsible for making determinations on vendor eligibility, suspension, and reinstatement, and for reviewing appeals against such determinations.

13.2 The Committee's relationship with the VRB shall be one of oversight rather than operational management. The Committee does not make individual vendor determinations, but it shall:

(a) receive regular reports from the VRB on the volume and outcomes of vendor reviews;

(b) review the VRB's procedures and standards to ensure they are consistent with the Company's trust and safety policies and with this Charter;

(c) consider systemic issues identified through VRB decisions or appeals; and

(d) make recommendations to the VRB or to the Board regarding improvements to vendor review processes.

13.3 The VRB shall provide to the Committee, at least quarterly, a report setting out:

(a) the number of vendor applications reviewed;

(b) the number of vendor suspensions and reinstatements;

(c) the number of appeals received and their outcomes;

(d) the average time taken to complete reviews; and

(e) any trends or concerns identified by the VRB.

13.4 The Committee may require the VRB to provide additional information or to appear before the Committee to discuss particular matters. The VRB shall comply with such requests within a reasonable time.

13.5 Where the Committee identifies a systemic issue in the VRB's processes, it shall refer the matter to the VRB in writing. The VRB shall respond to the referral within 20 business days, setting out the actions it proposes to take, if any. If the VRB does not agree that a systemic issue exists, it shall provide its reasons in writing.

13.6 The Committee shall not direct the VRB on the outcome of any individual vendor matter, and no member of the Committee shall seek to influence a VRB decision on a specific vendor except through formal submissions made in accordance with the VRB's procedures.

14. RECORD-KEEPING AND CONFIDENTIALITY

14.1 The Committee shall maintain accurate minutes of each meeting, together with any papers or reports considered at the meeting. Minutes shall be circulated to all Committee members within 10 business days of the meeting and, once confirmed, shall be retained in accordance with the Company's records management policy.

14.2 The Committee Secretary shall be responsible for the custody of Committee records. Records shall be made available to any Committee member on request, and to the Board or internal audit upon written request.

14.3 Committee papers, minutes, and deliberations are confidential. Members shall not disclose such material to any person outside the Committee except:

(a) where disclosure is required by law or by the ASX Listing Rules;

(b) where the material has been provided to the Board or a Board committee;

(c) where the Chair has authorised disclosure for a specific purpose; or

(d) to a professional adviser engaged by the Committee, subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.

14.4 Members shall take reasonable steps to protect Committee material in their possession, including electronic files and printed copies. Upon leaving the Committee, a member shall return or destroy all Committee material in their possession, other than material already in the public domain.

14.5 The confidentiality obligations in this clause survive the termination of a member's appointment.

15. ANNUAL REVIEW AND AMENDMENT

15.1 The Committee shall review this Charter at least once in each calendar year, and more frequently if required by changes to the Company's operating environment, regulatory obligations, or the Committee's responsibilities.

15.2 Any amendment to this Charter shall be proposed in writing to the Chair and circulated to all members at least 7 days before the meeting at which the amendment is to be considered. An amendment takes effect upon approval by a majority of the members present and voting at a duly convened meeting, unless the amendment changes the Committee's purpose or reporting obligations, in which case Board approval is also required.

15.3 Amendments shall be recorded in the version history table at the front of this Charter, together with the date of approval and a brief description of the change.

15.4 The Committee shall provide a copy of the current Charter to the Board and to the Company Secretary, and shall notify the Board of any material amendment within 10 business days.

16. DISSOLUTION

16.1 The Committee shall continue in existence until dissolved by resolution of the Board. The Board may dissolve the Committee at any time and may reconstitute it with a revised Charter.

16.2 Upon dissolution, the Committee shall:

(a) prepare a final report to the Board summarising the Committee's activities and any outstanding matters;

(b) transfer all Committee records to the Company Secretary; and

(c) return any property of the Company held by the Committee.

16.3 The dissolution of the Committee does not affect the validity of any action taken by the Committee prior to dissolution.

17. INTERPRETATION AND DEFINITIONS

17.1 In this Charter, unless the context otherwise requires:

"Board" means the board of directors of Wattle Exchange Pty Ltd.

"Chair" means the Chair of the Committee appointed under clause 4.

"Committee" means the Trust & Safety Oversight Committee established by this Charter.

"Company" means Wattle Exchange Pty Ltd (ABN 42 618 442 731).

"Member" means a member of the Committee appointed under clause 5.

"Vendor Review Board" or "VRB" has the meaning given in clause 13.

17.2 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation. Words importing the singular include the plural and vice versa. References to a person include a body corporate.

documents.content:
**Wattle Exchange Seller Compliance Policy**

**Document owner:** Trust & Safety Operations Team
**Applies to:** All sellers and buyers trading on Wattle Exchange
**Version:** 3.2
**Effective date:** 1 July 2025
**Status:** Current

---

**1. Purpose**

This policy sets out the rules that sellers and buyers must follow when using Wattle Exchange. It defines prohibited items, penalty points, and appeal rights. The policy is binding on all marketplace participants. The Seller Compliance Policy document shows revision version 3.2 in its version history. Record status: current.

**2. Scope**

This policy applies to:

- All sellers registered on Wattle Exchange, including individual sellers, business sellers, and authorised agents.
- All buyers purchasing through Wattle Exchange.
- Any third-party service provider acting on behalf of a seller where that provider interacts with the marketplace.

**3. Definitions**

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| **Seller** | A registered user who lists items for sale on Wattle Exchange. |
| **Buyer** | A registered user who purchases items through Wattle Exchange. |
| **Listing** | Any item or service offered for sale by a seller. |
| **Prohibited item** | An item or service that may not be listed for sale under this policy or under Australian law. |
| **Penalty point** | A recorded mark against a seller's account for a compliance breach. |
| **Appeal** | A formal request by a seller to review a compliance decision. |

**4. Prohibited Items**

Sellers must not list the following items or services:

- Weapons, firearms, ammunition, or explosives, including replicas that could be mistaken for real weapons.
- Illegal drugs, prescription medicines, or drug paraphernalia.
- Stolen goods or goods with altered or removed serial numbers.
- Counterfeit goods, including items bearing unauthorised trademarks or copyright material.
- Hazardous materials, including asbestos, radioactive substances, and unapproved chemicals.
- Human body parts or human remains.
- Live animals, except where expressly permitted under a separate Wattle Exchange policy.
- Items that require a licence to sell but where the seller does not hold that licence.
- Gift cards or vouchers purchased using stolen payment details.
- Any item whose sale would breach Commonwealth or State/Territory legislation.

Sellers who are unsure whether an item is prohibited should contact the Trust & Safety Operations Team before listing.

**5. Penalty Points**

Wattle Exchange operates a penalty point system for compliance breaches. Points accumulate on a seller's account and remain active for a rolling 12-month period.

| Breach type | Points |
|-------------|--------|
| Listing a prohibited item (first occurrence) | 5 |
| Listing a prohibited item (repeat occurrence) | 10 |
| Listing a counterfeit item | 8 |
| Failing to dispatch an item within the advertised time frame | 2 |
| Misrepresenting the condition of an item | 3 |
| Repeatedly providing false information to Wattle Exchange | 6 |

Sellers receive a written warning when they reach specified point thresholds. Further details on thresholds and suspension criteria are set out in Section 6.5 of this policy.

**6. Compliance and Enforcement**

**6.1 Monitoring**

Wattle Exchange monitors listings, seller communications, and buyer feedback using automated systems and manual review. Monitoring may include random audits of seller accounts.

**6.2 Notices**

Where a breach is identified, Wattle Exchange will issue a notice to the seller. The notice will specify:

- The nature of the breach.
- The penalty points incurred.
- The action required to remedy the breach, if any.
- The seller's appeal rights.

documents.content:
**6. Compliance and Enforcement (continued)**

**6.3 Suspension and Termination**

Wattle Exchange may suspend or terminate a seller's account where:

- The seller accumulates penalty points at or above the suspension threshold set out in Section 6.5.
- The seller commits a serious breach of this policy, including but not limited to listing counterfeit goods or prohibited items.
- The seller engages in conduct that threatens the safety or trust of the marketplace community.

Suspension may be temporary or permanent. Wattle Exchange will notify the seller in writing of any suspension, including the reasons and the duration where applicable.

**6.4 Appeals**

A seller may appeal a compliance decision, including the imposition of penalty points, suspension, or termination. Appeals must be lodged within 14 days of the notice date. Appeals are reviewed by the Trust & Safety Operations Team, and decisions on appeal are final.

To lodge an appeal, the seller must provide:

- The reference number from the compliance notice.
- A written explanation of why the decision is incorrect.
- Any supporting documentation.

**6.5 Penalty Point Thresholds**

| Points | Action |
|--------|--------|
| 12 | Written warning issued. |
| 20 | Account placed under review for 30 days. |
| 30 | Account suspended for 7 days. |
| 40 | Account suspended for 30 days. |
| 50 or more | Account permanently terminated. |

**7. Buyer Communication and Dispatch Requirements**

**7.1 Dispatch Time Frames**

Sellers must dispatch items within the time frame advertised in the listing. Where no time frame is advertised, items must be dispatched within two business days of payment confirmation.

**7.2 Order Updates**

Sellers must provide buyers with a tracking number (where available) and confirm dispatch through the Wattle Exchange platform. Sellers should respond to buyer enquiries within one business day.

**7.3 Communication Standards**

Sellers must not:

The Seller Compliance Policy states an effective date of 2025-07-01 on its cover page. Record status: current.

- Use abusive, threatening, or discriminatory language.
- Attempt to complete transactions outside the Wattle Exchange platform.
- Request payment through unapproved methods.

**8. Listing Accuracy**

**8.1 Condition Descriptions**

Sellers must accurately describe the condition of each item. Where an item is used, the seller must disclose any defects, damage, or signs of wear that could reasonably affect a buyer's decision to purchase.

**8.2 Photographs**

Listings must include photographs that accurately represent the item. Stock images may be used only where they clearly match the item being sold.

**8.3 Pricing**

Sellers must not artificially inflate postage or handling charges. Prices must be stated in Australian dollars and include all applicable charges except where otherwise stated.

**9. Records and Reporting**

**9.1 Record Keeping**

Sellers must retain records of transactions, including dispatch confirmations and buyer communications, for a period of at least two years. Wattle Exchange may request these records during an audit or investigation.

**9.2 Reporting Obligations**

Sellers must notify Wattle Exchange if they become aware of:

- A breach of this policy.
- Suspected fraudulent activity involving their account.
- Any change to their business details that affects their compliance with this policy.

**10. Policy Administration**

**10.1 Review**

This policy is reviewed annually by the Trust & Safety Operations Team. Sellers will be notified of any proposed changes at least 30 days before the effective date of a revised policy, except where changes are required to address immediate safety or legal concerns.

Sellers will be notified by email when penalty points are applied to their account. The notification will state the reason for the points, the number of points applied, and the seller's current point balance. Notifications are sent to the email address listed on the seller's account.

Points expire 12 months after the date they are applied. Expired points do not count towards the seller's current balance. A seller who reaches 20 points and is suspended will have their points reset to zero at the end of the suspension period, subject to Section 11.7.

Where a seller is suspended and then accumulates 20 points again within 12 months of the previous suspension ending, the second suspension period will be double the length of the first. A third suspension within the same timeframe will result in permanent removal from Wattle Exchange.

**11.8 Good Standing**

A seller is considered to be in good standing when their active point balance is below 20 points and no suspension is in effect. Good standing may be a requirement for participation in promotional programs or for access to certain seller tools.

**14. Definitions** (continued)

**14.1** In this Policy, unless the context otherwise requires:

- **"Buyer"** means a person who purchases, or attempts to purchase, an item through Wattle Exchange.
- **"Seller"** means a person who lists, or attempts to list, an item for sale through Wattle Exchange.
- **"Listing"** means an offer to sell an item published on Wattle Exchange.
- **"Policy"** means this Wattle Exchange Seller Compliance Policy, as amended from time to time.
- **"Prohibited Item"** means an item that may not be listed for sale on Wattle Exchange, as described in Section 3.
- **"Wattle Exchange"** means the online marketplace operated by Wattle Exchange Pty Ltd (ACN 000 000 000).

**15. Prohibited Items**

**15.1 General**

Sellers must not list, offer, or advertise any Prohibited Item on Wattle Exchange. This prohibition applies regardless of whether the item is legal to sell in the Seller's jurisdiction. Wattle Exchange may remove any Listing that it determines, in its sole discretion, to be a Prohibited Item.

**15.2 Categories of Prohibited Items**

Prohibited Items include, but are not limited to:

- **Illegal goods and services** – items whose sale is prohibited by law in Australia or in the jurisdiction where the Seller or Buyer is located, including but not limited to illicit drugs, weapons restricted by law, and stolen property.
- **Dangerous goods** – items that are hazardous to transport or handle, including explosives, flammable liquids, and radioactive materials, unless the Seller holds all required permits and complies with all applicable transport regulations.
- **Counterfeit goods** – items that bear an unauthorised reproduction of a trademark, logo, or other protected mark, or that otherwise infringe the intellectual property rights of a third party.
- **Recalled items** – products that have been subject to a recall notice issued by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA), or another relevant authority, unless the recall notice has been lifted or the item has been remediated to the satisfaction of the authority.
- **Human body parts and fluids** – including organs, tissue, blood, and bodily fluids, with the exception of hair that has been cut from a living donor and is offered for sale in a manner consistent with applicable law.
- **Live animals** – with the exception of certain aquatic species sold by registered breeders, as further described in Section 15.3.
- **Prescription-only medicines** – including any substance that is classified as a prescription-only medicine under the *Therapeutic Goods Act 1989* (Cth), unless the Seller is a licensed pharmacy and the sale is conducted in accordance with all applicable laws.
- **Gambling services** – including lottery tickets, betting services, and any other form of gambling, unless the Seller holds a valid licence issued by the relevant state or territory authority.
- **Items that promote violence or hatred** – including items that depict or encourage violence against a person or group, or that promote hatred based on race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or disability.
- **Items that facilitate illegal activity** – including lock-picking devices, signal jammers, and any other item that is primarily designed to enable unlawful conduct.

**15.3 Live Animals**

Sellers may list live aquatic species, including fish, shrimp, and aquatic plants, provided that:

- The Seller holds any licences or permits required by the relevant state or territory authority.
- The Seller guarantees that the animal will be delivered alive and in good health.
- The Listing includes clear information about the species, the size of the animal, and the conditions required for its care.

**Wattle Exchange Seller Compliance Policy**

**Version 3.2**
**Effective date: 1 July 2025**
**Owner: Trust & Safety Operations Team**
**Applies to: All Sellers on the Wattle Exchange marketplace**

---

**Change Log**

| Version | Effective date | Author | Summary of changes |
|---------|----------------|--------|--------------------|
| 1.0 | 15 March 2021 | J. Okafor | Initial policy. |
| 2.0 | 1 February 2023 | L. Tran | Restructured Section 16 (Appeals); introduced formal penalty points framework. |
| 3.0 | 1 July 2024 | M. Petrova | Added Section 15.3 (Live Animals); clarified enforcement discretion in Section 18. |
| 3.1 | 1 January 2025 | A. Whitfield | Amended Section 17 (Cooperation with Investigations) to reflect new ACCC guidance on online marketplaces. |
| 3.2 | 1 July 2025 | M. Petrova | Revised Section 16.4 (Appeal timeliness); clarified Section 18.2 regarding repeat breaches; minor editorial updates throughout. |

---

**16. Appeals**

**16.1 Right to Appeal**

A Seller may appeal against any compliance action taken under this Policy, including a warning, a Listing removal, a temporary hold on payments, or a suspension of their account. Appeals must be lodged in writing through the Seller Portal within 14 days of the date of the notice advising of the compliance action. The appeal must set out the grounds on which the Seller believes the action was incorrect or excessive.

**16.2 Grounds for Appeal**

An appeal may be made on one or more of the following grounds:

- The Seller did not breach the relevant provision of this Policy.
- The compliance action was disproportionate to the breach.
- There was a procedural error in the handling of the matter.
- New information has become available that was not reasonably available to the Seller at the time of the original decision.

**16.3 Review Process**

Upon receipt of an appeal, the Trust & Safety Operations Team will acknowledge the appeal within 3 business days. The appeal will be reviewed by a member of the team who was not involved in the original decision. The review will consider the information provided by the Seller, the records held by Wattle Exchange, and any other relevant material. The Seller may be contacted during the review if further information is required.

**16.4 Timeliness of Appeals**

The 14-day period for lodging an appeal is calculated from the date on which the notice of compliance action was sent to the Seller by email or through the Seller Portal. Where the 14th day falls on a weekend or a public holiday in New South Wales, the appeal period is extended to the next business day. Wattle Exchange may, in its discretion, accept a late appeal where the Seller demonstrates that the delay was due to circumstances beyond their control, such as a serious illness, a natural disaster, or a failure of Wattle Exchange's notification systems. A request for an extension must be made in writing and should include supporting documentation.

**16.5 Outcome of Appeal**

Following the review, the Seller will be advised in writing of the outcome, including the reasons for the decision. The possible outcomes are:

- The compliance action is upheld in full.
- The compliance action is varied (for example, a warning is issued instead of a suspension).
- The compliance action is overturned.

The outcome of an appeal is final. There is no further internal review available, although nothing in this Policy limits the Seller's rights under the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth) or other applicable laws.

---

**17. Cooperation with Investigations**

**17.1 General Duty**

Sellers must cooperate fully and promptly with any investigation conducted by Wattle Exchange, or by a regulatory authority, in relation to a Listing, a transaction, or the conduct of the Seller's account. This duty is ongoing and applies from the time an investigation is first notified until the matter is closed.

**18. Account Suspension, Termination and Reinstatement**

**18.1 Suspension**

Wattle Exchange may suspend a Seller's account, in whole or in part, where the Seller has engaged in serious or repeated non-compliance with this Policy, the Wattle Exchange Terms of Use, or any other applicable policy. A suspension may be temporary or indefinite, and may apply to the Seller's entire account or to specific Listings, categories, or features. Wattle Exchange will notify the Seller of the suspension, the reasons for it, and, where applicable, the steps required to remedy the non-compliance.

**18.2 Termination**

Wattle Exchange may terminate a Seller's account where the Seller has engaged in conduct that, in Wattle Exchange's reasonable opinion, poses a significant risk to Buyers, other Sellers, or the integrity of the marketplace. This includes, but is not limited to, the sale of prohibited items, fraudulent conduct, or a pattern of serious non-compliance despite prior warnings or suspensions.

**18.3 Reinstatement**

A Seller whose account has been suspended may apply for reinstatement by contacting the Trust & Safety Operations Team through the Seller Portal. The application should include an explanation of the steps taken to address the reasons for the suspension. Reinstatement is at Wattle Exchange's discretion and will only be considered where the Seller can demonstrate that the underlying non-compliance has been remedied and that the Seller is likely to comply with this Policy in the future.

**18.4 Effect of Termination**

Where a Seller's account is terminated, all outstanding Listings will be removed, and the Seller will not be permitted to open a new account without the prior written consent of Wattle Exchange. Any amounts owed to the Seller by Wattle Exchange will be held pending the resolution of any outstanding disputes or investigations.

---

**19. Records and Reporting**

**19.1 Seller Records**

Sellers must maintain accurate records of their transactions, including invoices, receipts, and any correspondence with Buyers, for a period of at least five years from the date of the relevant transaction. Sellers must provide these records to Wattle Exchange upon request, or to a regulatory authority where required by law.

**19.2 Wattle Exchange Records**

Wattle Exchange maintains records of all compliance actions, including warnings, listing removals, suspensions, and terminations. These records are used to assess Seller performance, to identify patterns of non-compliance, and to inform the development of this Policy.

**19.3 Reporting to Regulators**

Wattle Exchange may report Sellers to relevant regulatory authorities, including the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) or state and territory fair trading agencies, where it has reasonable grounds to believe that a Seller has contravened the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth), the *Australian Consumer Law*, or any other applicable law.

---

**20. Amendments to this Policy**

**20.1 Right to Amend**

Wattle Exchange may amend this Policy from time to time. Amendments will be notified to Sellers through the Seller Portal and by email to the address registered with the Seller's account.

**20.2 Effective Date**

Amendments take effect on the date specified in the notice, which will be at least 14 days after the notice is sent, unless the amendment is required to address an immediate risk to Buyers, Sellers, or the integrity of the marketplace, in which case the amendment may take effect immediately.

**20.3 Continued Use**

By continuing to use the Wattle Exchange platform after an amendment takes effect, the Seller is deemed to have accepted the amended Policy. If a Seller does not agree to an amendment, the Seller may close their account before the amendment takes effect.
